attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pT2 stage, positive surgical margins, and the presence of lymph node metastasis. Conversely, the absence of extraprostatic extension and invasion of the seminal vesicles are favorable findings. The biopsy demonstrated a Gleason 3+4 diagnosis, which aligns with the surgical finding.

The nodal status is documented as positive lymph node metastasis. The difference between the biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted, though the specific histological pattern reported was Acinar. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly widens the uncertainty regarding the trajectory of the disease. The current horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 68.6 months without an event. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent changes would be crucial in refining this prognosis.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage pT2, Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), positive surgical margins, and lymph node metastasis present. The seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The preoperative PSA was 4.1. The surgical findings include positive margins and the presence of lymph node metastasis, which are factors driving the prognosis. The biopsy grade was Gleason 3+4, which was consistent with the surgical specimen.

Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and the absence of lymphovascular invasion. The nodal status was documented as metastasis present. The preoperative PSA of 4.1 is a relevant factor. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up information would revise the prognosis and its subsequent trajectory. The current prognostic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 68.56688349808537 months without an event.
